recommendation: Keep the no-change audit. If the work group wants a new current-model example for multiple simultaneous operators, treat that as a separate design decision, likely using Group or CareTeam rather than reviving the removed operation backbone.
issue_request: FHIR-40455 was Applied/Persuasive with Modification for R6 after being raised against R5. It requested adding DeviceAssociation examples such as an implant assigned to a patient with an open period and body site, wheelchair assigned to a patient with a future end date, tablet assigned to a provider, surgical robot/patient/operator period, blood pressure monitor during an in-patient stay, and lab device calibration without a patient.
initial_application: The issue was applied by July 2025 commits 63aa9cc407, a8ca8f5230, 9840cc6ef0, 8c67215155, and fa2f8f096f, which added the six DeviceAssociation example XML files and registered them in source/deviceassociation/list-DeviceAssociation-examples.xml. Jira comments in July and October 2025 confirm the examples were reviewed and listed in the build.
additional_context: DeviceAssociation is active in source/fhir.ini and the example files under source/deviceassociation are current build inputs. Later Applied issue FHIR-47604 removed the operation/operator backbone, added focus, and moved operator semantics to relationship=operator with associationStatus and period; its Jira discussion notes that prior examples with two operators are no longer viable under the new focus cardinality. Current StructureDefinition guidance directs multiple simultaneous individuals to Group or CareTeam.
reconciliation: Published an empty audit commit because no source edit is needed. Current source already contains all six requested example categories and the examples use the later, current DeviceAssociation subject/focus/relationship/associationStatus model rather than the removed operation backbone.

related_jiras.note: Changed DeviceAssociation operator modeling after FHIR-40455 and explains why the current examples no longer preserve the original two-operator operation block.
